principle: State identities modify role-specific kernels modestly; national strength also depends on manpower, quality distributions, commanders, doctrine, terrain, logistics, morale, and experience.

states.QIN: Best-balanced institutional army: disciplined line infantry, command, training, logistics, and combined-arms coordination.
states.ZHAO: Cavalry and frontier warfare leader: superior riding, scouting, maneuver, field experience, and mobile command.
states.WEI: Technical warfare specialist: crossbows, siege engineering, chariots, fortifications, and deliberate tactical systems.
states.CHU: Massive, physically powerful and regionally varied: stronger heavy fighting base but less uniformly centralized administration.
states.YAN: Frontier and mountain-oriented: cavalry, bows, scouts, survival, and terrain knowledge exceed its generic line quality.
states.QI: Wealthy, organized defensive state: logistics, training, administration, missile support, and strategic patience.
states.HAN: Smallest state: weaker broad manpower quality offset by unusually strong crossbow, engineering, and fortified-defense specialization.
